---
name: used-car-scout
description: >-
  Use this when the owner wants to find a reliable used car near them, check
  what's for sale within a budget, re-run or schedule their used-car search, or
  asks "anything good on the used market?" Searches Craigslist (no key) and
  optionally Auto.dev dealer listings and public auction pages, estimates miles
  left per car (by default requiring 50k+ more, within 50 miles; both optional),
  ranks them by confidence tier, writes an HTML report plus a Markdown copy, and
  saves them to the owner's chosen destination. Report-only; never contacts
  sellers.
---
# Used car scout

Finds used cars near the owner's US ZIP (within a hard radius, default 50 miles, optional), under a
price cap (one `any` cap for all makes, or per make), and estimates how many miles each car has left
(enforcing a minimum, default **50,000+ more miles**, optional). Output is a self-contained HTML report plus a Markdown
copy (dated files + `latest.html` / `latest.md`, optional CSV). The bot **only reports**: it never messages sellers, books test
drives, makes offers, or pays for anything.

## Before you run

1. Read the owner's saved settings from memory (set by the `used-car-scout-getting-started` skill):
   ZIP, price cap (one `any` cap or per make), and optionally radius, model list, min miles left,
   report destination, whether they use Auto.dev.
   If they're missing, run that skill first. **ZIP and price are required and have no default**;
   never guess them (the script refuses to run without them and says what's missing). Everything else
   has a default: radius 50 mi (blank/0 = any distance), makes/models any (all makes:
   `price_caps: {any: <price>}`), min miles left 50,000 (blank/0 = no longevity cutoff), min price
   $4,000, private sellers only, no CSV, no auctions, reports in the working folder.
2. Set up the script: follow **Get the script** below to download `ucs.py` into a working folder and
   check its hash (it's self-contained; `uv` installs its dependencies from the inline header).
   Then run `uv run ucs.py --init-config scout.yaml` for a commented starter and edit it from the
   saved settings: fill in `zip` and replace `<YOUR_MAX_PRICE>` under `price_caps` (the only two
   required edits). Change other fields only where the saved settings differ from the defaults
   (for example `radius_miles`, `min_miles_left`, `purveyor: all` for dealers too, `csv: true`).
   Leave `output_dir` blank: reports then land in the folder you run the script from. You can pass
   flags instead of a config.
3. Auto.dev is optional. If the owner stored an Auto.dev key as a secret, expose it to the run as the
   `AUTO_DEV_API_KEY` environment variable. Never print it, never write it into the config, the report
   or chat. The starter's `autodev.enabled: auto` uses Auto.dev only when that variable is set; with no
   key, the script skips Auto.dev and says so in the report. If the owner has Auto.dev off, run without
   the variable (or set `enabled: false`).

## Run

```bash
uv run ucs.py --config scout.yaml
# or everything on the command line (<MAX_PRICE> = the owner's saved cap, e.g. 12000):
uv run ucs.py --zip <ZIP> --cap any=<MAX_PRICE>     # all makes, 50 mi, 50k+ left, reports in this folder
uv run ucs.py --zip <ZIP> --radius 30 --cap toyota=<PRICE> --cap honda=<PRICE> \
  --models camry,corolla,civic --min-miles-left 100000 --out <REPORT_FOLDER> --csv
```

Useful flags: `--radius 30` (hard cutoff; default 50, `0` = any distance), `--min-miles-left 100000` (hard cutoff; default 50000, `0` = none), `--top 8`, `--year-min`, `--min-price`,
`--out <folder>` (default: the current folder), `--no-craigslist`, `--no-autodev`, `--no-md` (skip the Markdown copy; config `md: true` by default),
`--csv`, `--detail-pages 30`, `--auction-url URL --auction-zip ZIP`
(repeatable; public auction list pages are **off unless the owner supplies them**).
Config-only: `manual_check_links` (list of `{url, label, note}`) adds a "check by hand" list to the
report for sites that can't be scraped.

A run takes about 1–2 minutes (polite ~1.5 s delay between requests). Afterward, open
`latest.md` (or `latest.html`) and give the owner a short summary: counts per source, how many
passed, the top picks (year/make/model, price, miles, est. miles left, distance, confidence), any
notable cars with no lifespan data (est. miles left unknown), and any source that failed. Offer the report file; don't paste the whole table.
**First run:** the report and console say "First run: this sets the baseline; later runs mark new
cars and price drops." Pass that on, so the owner knows nothing is marked new yet.

## Save the reports

The script writes into its working folder on the bot's computer (or `output_dir` / `--out` if set).
Keep running from the same folder so the new/price-drop tracking works. Then copy the dated HTML and
Markdown files (and CSVs if on) to wherever the saved settings say. Typical destinations:

- **Bot workspace (the default):** leave the files where they are and attach the HTML report in chat.
- **iCloud Drive via a registered Mac:** copy each file with CopyFromBox to
  `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/<folder>/used-car-scout/` on that Mac (create the
  subfolder first if needed). The Mac must be online; if it isn't, say so and keep the files on
  the bot's computer.
- **Google Drive:** upload each file to the saved Drive folder with the Drive upload tool.
- **A folder on a registered computer:** copy each file there with CopyFromBox.

Tell the owner where the files landed. If a save fails, report it and give the local path instead.

## What the script enforces

- **Radius (optional, default 50 mi)**: straight-line distance from the ZIP center to each listing's own
  coordinates and/or ZIP centroid (Census ZCTA data, downloaded once); if both exist, the farther
  one is used. No location = excluded. Distance is shown for every car. With a radius set, it's a
  hard cutoff (default 50 mi); set blank/0 for none, and searches use ~100 mi and nothing is cut by distance.
- **Price caps (required, no default)**: `any: <price>` applies one cap to **all makes** (header reads "Any make ≤ $X"): Craigslist
  (and Auto.dev) are searched for every car in the price range with no make filter, and the Craigslist
  JSON search API fills in odometers so most cars get an estimate without opening each listing. A per-make
  cap next to `any` overrides it for that make. Per-make caps alone limit the search to those makes.
  At least one numeric cap is required; with none (or the starter's `<YOUR_MAX_PRICE>` placeholder
  left in), the script stops with "Can't run yet. Missing required setting(s): …".
- **Min miles left (optional, default 50,000)**: est. miles left = low end of typical lifespan for the model with good
  maintenance − odometer − known weak points. Lifespan estimates cover most US-market makes and their main
  models (Toyota, Lexus, Honda, Acura, Mazda, Tesla, Scion, Subaru, Nissan, Infiniti, Hyundai, Kia, Genesis,
  Mitsubishi, Ford, Chevrolet, GMC, Ram, Dodge, Jeep, Chrysler, Buick, Cadillac, Lincoln, Mercury, Pontiac,
  Volkswagen, Audi, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, Mini, Porsche, Land Rover, Jaguar). They are conservative
  low-end figures informed by Consumer Reports reliability surveys, iSeeCars longest-lasting studies and
  RepairPal ratings. They are rules of thumb, not measured stats (adjust with `lifespan_overrides`).
  Weak-point deductions by year range include: Honda 2014–16 CVT −30k; Honda V6 VCM 2008–13 −20k; hybrid
  pack 8–11 yrs −20k, 12+ yrs −40k; Tesla pack warranty expired −40k / nearly up −20k; 2014–16 Model S/X
  −40k; Nissan CVTs 2013–18 −30k; Ford PowerShift DPS6 (Focus/Fiesta 2011/12–16) −40k; Ford 5.4 3V cam
  phasers 2004–10 −25k; Ford 6.0/6.4 diesel −40k; Hyundai/Kia Theta II 2011–19 −30k; GM AFM/DFM V8 lifters
  2007–21 −20k; GM 2.4 oil consumption (Equinox/Terrain 2010–17, Malibu 2010–13) −30k; Cruze 1.4T 2011–16
  −20k; GM 3.6 timing chain −20k; Northstar −30k; Subaru EJ25 head gaskets before 2012 −25k; BMW N20 2012–15
  −30k; VW/Audi 2.0T 2008–12 −30k; ZF 9-speed 2014–17 −20k; Porsche IMS −30k; Mini Prince 1.6 −20k. Mazda
  has no major one in these years.
  **With `any`:** a model of a known make that isn't listed individually uses a conservative make average,
  labeled "make-average estimate". Titles that name only the model ("2018 Civic EX", "1995 Neon") get
  their make from the model name, including common older names not in the lifespan table (Neon,
  Cavalier, Celica, Grand Am, Rodeo and the like; only when the title has a year). Years written with
  an apostrophe ("'82", "07 '") count as model years. Only makes with no data at all (and listings where no make can be
  identified) are "unrated". Those cars are **kept, never cut by the miles-left minimum**, labeled
  **"no lifespan data — est. miles left unknown"**, given low (low-info) confidence, and sorted below every
  rated car that passes. **A rated or make-average car whose listing gives no odometer or year is
  excluded** while a miles-left cutoff is set (the report lists it under "odometer/year not in
  listing"), because its miles left can't be checked. Odometers implausibly low for the car's age (for example "1,000 mi" on a 30-year-old truck) are flagged
  and sorted after credible cars.
  **With per-make caps only:** unrated models and listings with no odometer are excluded when a cutoff is
  set. With no cutoff (blank/0), they're kept and marked low-info (est. miles left "—") and sort after
  rated cars in their tier. Est. miles left is shown for every car (or "unknown").
- **Not a regular car** = skipped: special-purpose vehicles (hearses, limos, ambulances, buses/coaches,
  fire/tow/box/dump trucks, RVs and camper vans), powersports and trailers (Can-Am, ATVs, motorcycles), heavy trucks
  (International 4300-class, Freightliner, etc.) and engine/transmission-only listings.
- **Reposts**: the same car listed twice under different titles (same year, make and model, odometer
  within 1,000 mi, price within 5%) is merged into one row, keeping the lower price (or the newer post),
  and the report notes the merge. With `any`, a few common misspellings and glued-on suffixes are
  normalized so the model still matches (e.g. "Camey" → Camry, "focus52km" → Focus).
- **Branded titles** (salvage, rebuilt, flood) mentioned in a listing = excluded. Scam-ish or as-is
  language and suspiciously low prices are flagged, not excluded.
- **Confidence is a tier, not a penalty.** high = history report with 0 accidents → medium =
  history report with accidents → low = no history (private sale, auction, dealer with no history
  data). Picks take all high, then medium; low-confidence cars only fill leftover slots and are
  labeled "LOW CONFIDENCE". Within a tier, cars are ordered by value (price, miles, est. miles left).
- **New / price drop**: the first run into a folder sets the baseline (nothing is marked new). Later
  runs into the same folder mark cars as **new** or **price drop** (small `.ucs-seen.json`).

## Scheduling

Only if the owner asks: offer a daily or weekly run and confirm the time first. Don't set one up
on your own. On a scheduled run, lead the summary with new cars and price drops.

## Caveats (tell the owner when relevant)

- **Auto.dev is a paid API after its free trial.** Without a key (or after the trial ends, which
  shows up as HTTP 401/402/403 in the source notes) the scout runs Craigslist-only. Craigslist-only
  results are all low confidence because private listings have no history report.
- **Craigslist is best-effort.** It reads public pages. Search pages are now built by JavaScript,
  so when the static HTML has no listings the script falls back to the page's JSON-LD data, then
  to the JSON search API the page itself uses (the note shows "via search API"). Craigslist can block
  automated access (HTTP 403) or change its layout at any time, and the report says when that
  happens. Keep the request rate low and don't loop runs.
- Auction pages vary a lot. Parsing is heuristic, many sites are JavaScript-only (need a manual
  check), bids are not final, and buyer premiums are extra.
- **Price cap is listing price, not total cost.** `price_caps` is checked against the advertised
  (or current bid) price only; sales tax, title/registration, dealer doc fees, and auction buyer
  premiums are on top. If the owner means the cap as a hard total spend, say so and ask whether
  to lower the listing cap to leave a buffer — do not silently treat the two as the same.
- Lifespans and deductions are rules of thumb, not a guarantee. The report is a screen, not a buy
  signal: tell the owner to get a history report and a pre-purchase inspection.
- US only (ZIP codes, Craigslist US).

## Get the script

`ucs.py` is published in 6 parts in a public GitHub repo:
https://github.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script . Download the parts in order, join them,
and check the SHA-256 before running anything. Run this in the working folder:

```bash
rm -f ucs.py
for u in \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part1.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part2.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part3.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part4.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part5.py \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jeffasu-ux/used-car-scout-script/ff328007982090229e32cb110837c7570309b535/ucs.part6.py \
; do curl -fsSL "$u" >> ucs.py; done
echo "91c27ca16e7fb00f74d8e4439509ddf5c00cb318a6c9ad93033edcfbde29fdf2  ucs.py" | sha256sum -c -
```

The URLs are pinned to one commit, so the script can't change under you. If `sha256sum`
doesn't print `ucs.py: OK` (or any download fails), **stop**: don't run the script, delete `ucs.py`,
and tell the owner the script download didn't match the expected version.

# Used car scout: getting started

Set up the owner's search once, then save it so every later run (and any schedule) uses the same
settings. On the first run, ask **exactly these four questions, in this order**, and nothing
else. ZIP and price limit are required and have **no default**; never guess them.

## Ask

1. **ZIP code** (required, no default). "What's your 5-digit US ZIP code?"
2. **Price limit** (required, no default). "What's the most you want to spend?" Take one cap for
   all makes, for example "up to $12,000", and save it as `any: 12000`. Mention they can set
   per-make caps later (for example, "Toyota up to $13,000, Honda up to $11,000").
3. **Miles left** (optional, default 50,000). "How many more miles do you need the car to last?"
   If they skip it, use 50,000. "No minimum" turns the cutoff off (every car still shows its estimate).
4. **Auto.dev key** (optional). "Do you have an Auto.dev API key?"
   - **Yes:** request it through the **secure secret input** and store it as a secret named
     `AUTO_DEV_API_KEY`. **Never ask them to paste it in chat.** If they paste it anyway, don't
     repeat it, and suggest they rotate it and re-enter it through the secure input.
   - **No:** recommend getting one. It adds dealer listings with history reports (accidents,
     owners), so there are more results and some reach high or medium confidence (Craigslist-only
     results are all low confidence). It's paid after a free trial, and they can add it later by
     running this skill again. Then continue without it.

## Defaults (don't ask)

Everything else uses these defaults, without asking:

- Radius **50 miles** (hard straight-line cutoff)
- **Any make/model** (all makes; cars with no lifespan data are still shown, labeled, and listed
  after rated cars)
- Minimum price **$4,000** (skips parts cars and scams)
- **Private sellers only** on Craigslist
- **No CSV** (HTML report plus a Markdown copy)
- **No auctions**
- Reports **saved in the bot workspace** and the HTML report **attached in chat**

After the four questions, tell them in one line that these defaults are in place and they can
change any of them later by just saying so, for example "search 30 miles", "save to iCloud" or
"dealers too".

## Save

Save one memory entry, "Used car scout settings", containing: ZIP, `price_caps` (`any: <price>`),
min miles left (50,000 if they skipped it, or "none"), `autodev: on (secret AUTO_DEV_API_KEY)` or
`autodev: off`, and the defaults above: radius 50, models any, min price 4000, purveyor owner,
CSV no, auctions none, report destination "bot workspace (attach HTML in chat)". **Never put the
key itself in memory.**

Then read the settings back in one short summary, offer a first run now (use the `used-car-scout`
skill; the first run sets the baseline, and later runs mark new cars and price drops), and ask
whether they'd like it to run on a schedule, such as daily or weekly at a time they pick. Set up a
schedule only if they say yes.

## Changing settings later

When the owner changes something, update that one field in the saved memory entry, confirm it,
and use it from the next run on. Ask a follow-up only when the change needs details:

- **Price:** "bump it to $14k" changes the `any` cap; "Toyota up to $15k" adds a per-make cap (it
  overrides `any` for that make; per-make caps alone limit the search to those makes).
- **Radius:** "search 30 miles" sets 30; "any distance" removes the cutoff (distance is still shown).
- **Makes/models:** specific makes (a cap per make) or models (for example Camry, Civic, CR-V).
- **Sellers:** "dealers too" sets purveyor all; "dealers only" sets dealer.
- **Min price, oldest model year, CSV, miles left:** set the field they name.
- **Where to save reports:**
  - **iCloud Drive** (readable on iPhone/iPad in the Files app): a folder under
    `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/` on one of their registered Macs. Ask which Mac
    and which folder (find it with a quick `ls` there and confirm), create a `used-car-scout`
    subfolder, and note the Mac must be on for saves to land.
  - **Google Drive**: a folder in their connected Drive (create "Used Car Scout" if they have no
    preference). Needs the Google Drive connector.
  - **A folder on one of their computers**: any path they name on a registered machine.
  - **Bot workspace** (the default): keep files on the bot's own computer and attach the HTML in chat.
  Confirm the exact destination back to them.
- **Auctions:** collect each public/municipal auction list-page URL and the lot's ZIP. Warn them
  that many auction sites need a manual check.
- **Auto.dev key:** add or replace it through the secure secret input only (question 4 above), or
  set `autodev: off` if they want it off.
